group_assessment.research_type_basis: Senior author Tanuma S (Dept of Biochemistry + Genome & Drug Research Center, Tokyo University of Science) has 259 PubMed records and exactly ONE on GSK (this paper), ZERO on WWOX. First author Saeki K has 2 on GSK. Methods are wet-lab and competent but standard: HEK293T co-expression, SDS-PAGE/Western, luminescent ATP-depletion kinase assay (Kinase-Glo), radiometric [gamma-32P]ATP in-vitro phosphorylation, deletion-mutant construction. No structural work, no neuronal model, no in-vivo work. This is a biochemistry lab making a single, well-controlled excursion into GSK-3 isoform biology.
group_assessment.method: NCBI eutils esearch counts, 2026-07-26: 'Tanuma S[au]' 259; 'Tanuma S[au] AND GSK' 1; 'Tanuma S[au] AND WWOX' 0; 'Saeki K[au] AND GSK' 2. Initial-form Japanese author names carry HIGH ambiguity; counts bound magnitude, they do not identify individuals.
group_assessment.weighting: The Saadane asymmetry applies in its favourable direction, and more cleanly than in either prior case. A laboratory with ZERO prior investment in GSK-3 isoform biology has no position to defend, so the OBSERVATION is strong as independent evidence. Normally the INTERPRETATION would be correspondingly weak from domain inexperience — but here it is unusually well protected, because the authors built two internal specificity controls into the design rather than asserting specificity: APP-Thr668 phosphorylation in cells (equivalent between isoforms) and pGS-2 peptide kinase activity in vitro (equivalent, and quantified: 234.5+-7.8 vs 246.5+-2.4 nmol/min/mg). Those controls convert 'beta2 is a weaker kinase' into 'tau specifically is an unfavourable substrate for beta2', which is a much stronger and much harder claim to reach by accident. Contrast with PMID 22193544, where the WWOX framing came from the field's founder and the interpretation was the stronger half: here the reverse holds — the data carry the weight, and the authors' own mechanistic proposal (CT higher-order structure) is explicitly offered as a hypothesis requiring a structure that does not exist.

queries.query: WWOX AND ("splice variant" OR isoform) AND GSK3

field_density.verdict: Six records in all of PubMed on the neuron-specific isoform itself. The isoform that Castano 2010 reports is REQUIRED for axon growth, that is enriched in growth cones, and that peaks in the developing brain, has been studied by essentially nobody. And the intersection this deep dive actually proposes — WWOX x GSK3 isoform — returns ZERO. That is the strongest emptiness measured in this model so far: not a contested question, an unasked one. Practical consequence: the decisive experiment (WWOX and WWOXtide against beta1 vs beta2 in parallel) has no competitor and no prior art to reconcile with.

corpus_crossquery.verdict: ZERO. Five files reason about GSK3beta — meta_index, meta_prenatal_structure, meta_network_myelin_glia, therapeutic_strategies (TX-005), claim_registry (CLAIM 016) — and every one of them treats it as a SINGLE enzyme. The distinction between a tau-phosphorylating, differentiation-blocking isoform and a growth-cone-enriched, axon-growth-promoting one is absent from the model, including from the file that scores lithium. This is not a gap in coverage, it is a category error propagated across the reasoning layer, and it was invisible until the reference list of PMID 22193544 was finally enumerated.

correction_made_this_run: This run CORRECTED an attribution error made by the preceding one. The PMID 22193544 session recorded, from the secondary review PMC3139124, that beta2 phosphorylates tau 'on different, partly overlapping residues' and treated Saeki 2011 as the primary source for it. Reading Saeki 2011 in full shows it tested ONE site only — Ser396 — and never addressed site selectivity. The different-sites claim traces to Mukai 2002 (PMID 12065620), still unread and now queued as FT-027. Verifying a secondary source at the primary is exactly what surfaced this, and Ser404 — the other site that matters in PMID 22193544 — remains untested by anyone.

verbatim_locators.source_fulltext_indexed_evidence: No PMCID and no open structured deposit. Europe PMC lists a Free PDF on J-STAGE and nothing else; there is no XML or HTML surface for this article anywhere, which under rule 5d puts it in the different class the rule requires to be declared rather than discovered a third time.
verbatim_locators.abstract_anchoring_waived: No locator is abstract-anchored and none could be. Every proposition below is either a panel reading or a bound on one — the unequal total-tau control, the unmatched titration series, the residue labels, the within-panel scope of the deletion experiment, the authors' own hypothesis marker. An abstract carries none of that.
verbatim_locators.unverifiable_reason: The text layer of files/fulltext/PMID21212533_Saeki2011.pdf is SUSPECT and is refused, correctly. It carries U+0002 for the multiplication sign and U+0003 for plus-minus, and it silently drops the micro sign, so 'means ± S.E.' extracts as 'means\x03S.E.' and '10 μl' extracts as '10 ml'. Roughly the same split rule 5d measured across the corpus: the visible half a sentinel catches, the printable half it never will. There is no structured surface to fall back to, so all fifteen locators are anchored to the printed page — each inside a crop that regenerates to its declared digest from the source PDF, and each text locator through a needle unique on its page. The needles are searched in the corrupt text layer on purpose: a needle is a coordinate, not a quotation, and the evidence is the crop.

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE PANEL, and it matters for how far the figure can be pushed: the total-tau control is NOT equal across lanes. In the beta1 lane the upper (retarded) tau band dominates and the lower band is depleted, the mobility shift expected of heavily phosphorylated tau, while mock and beta2 show both bands. There is no densitometry and no normalisation anywhere in this figure. The asymmetry runs AGAINST the paper's conclusion rather than with it — beta1 reaches more phospho-tau on less unshifted substrate — so the direction is safe; a fold-figure taken off this panel is not.

entries.proposition: POSITIVE CONTROL FOR RULE 5d, in the one class of damage no control character can catch. The printed page reads '10 microlitres of 2x SDS-PAGE sample buffer'. The extracted text layer of this PDF reads '10 ml of 2\x02 SDS-PAGE sample buffer': the multiplication sign became a C0 control, which a sentinel can see, and the micro sign was dropped outright, which no sentinel can see — leaving a volume wrong by a factor of a thousand in a sentence that still parses as English. This is why the surface is refused rather than repaired.

entries.proposition: The quantified half of the specificity argument, and the reason 'beta2 is a weak kinase' cannot stand: on the synthetic peptide pGS-2 the two isoforms are equally active, and beta2 is marginally the HIGHER of the two — 246.5 against 234.5 nmol/min/mg. Means +/- S.E. of three independent experiments; the table states no test and reports no p-value, so 'equivalent' here means overlapping, not tested. Both plus-minus signs are C0 control characters in the extracted text layer, which is why this is adjudicated on the page and not quoted from it.

entries.proposition: 🔴 BOUNDARY ON ANY FOLD-FIGURE TAKEN FROM FIGURE 3, and it corrects a number this model already carries. The two titration series are NOT matched: beta1 runs 0-0.1-0.3-1-3 and beta2 runs 0-0.3-1-3-10, so there is no shared top concentration and beta1 was never tested at 10. The lower aGSK-3b panel confirms enzyme only in the top lane or two of each series, so it is a presence check, not an equal-input control. There is no densitometry and the figure is 'representative of three independent experiments'. What the panel supports is beta1-at-1 versus beta2-at-10, i.e. of the order of ten-fold and plausibly more; what it cannot support is a measured ratio. DL-MECH-068 records '~3-10x', which reads as a measurement and is a visual estimate whose lower bound is wrong.

entries.proposition: 🔴 THE POSITION OF THE INSERT, READ FROM THE AUTHORS' OWN SCHEMATIC, and it disagrees with the third-party number this model recorded. Figure 4 marks the 13-amino-acid insert between residues labelled V303 and K304, gives the beta1 CT as 380-420 and the beta2 CT as 393-433, and the caption states the CT sequence is identical between the two. DL-MECH-068 cites UniProt P49841 VSP_004790 as 'K303', i.e. the lysine at 303 rather than at 304 — a one-residue disagreement in numbering convention between the primary figure and the database entry. Nothing load-bearing moves: on either numbering the insert sits four to five residues downstream of H299, immediately adjacent to the Axin/GID docking surface (G262-L273 + N285-H299) that WWOX binds, and far from the identical ATP site. The number should not be quoted as though the two sources agreed.

The GSK-3b1 bar ends 380 | 420 with a CT box; the GSK-3b2 bar ends 393 | 433 with a CT box and a black insert; the insertion point carries the labels V303 and K304; caption: 'The sequence of CT is identical between GSK-3b1 and GSK-3b2.'

entries.proposition: READ FROM THE PANEL — the deletion experiment, and the expression control makes it stronger than the sentence does. Left panel (beta1): ptau-Ser396 in the deltaCT lane is comparable to WT, while its aGSK-3b band is visibly WEAKER than WT — full tau phosphorylation at lower enzyme. Right panel (beta2): ptau-Ser396 in the deltaCT lane falls to about the mock level while its aGSK-3b band is strong. So the loss in beta2 is not loss of expression, and the retention in beta1 is not an expression advantage. 🔴 The two panels are separate blots: this figure compares WT with deltaCT WITHIN an isoform and licenses no beta1-versus-beta2 magnitude.
